summary.content:
Today's selection covers 63 articles from 8 trusted sources, including 32 on Artificial Intelligence and 16 on Fraud/Cybersecurity.

• **AI Spotlight**: Why Irregular’s A.I. Tests for Meta, Anthropic and OpenAI Went Off the Rails
• **Companies in Focus**: Coverage includes developments from OpenAI, Google, Anthropic
• **Security Alert**: Tricky 'SynkLoader' Multitool May Herald Ransomware
• **Threat Landscape**: Today's coverage highlights ransomware, phishing, data breaches
• **Source Diversity**: Articles sourced from NY Times Tech, The Verge, TechCrunch, Dark Reading, SecurityWeek and others
• **Fresh Content**: 39 articles published in the last 24 hours

top.title: Why Irregular’s A.I. Tests for Meta, Anthropic and OpenAI Went Off the Rails
top.description: Irregular, an Israeli start-up, worked with OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta to assess the security of their A.I. models. It made a mistake. Then the tests went off the rails.

top.title: OpenAI says its Jalapeño chip can power faster AI responses than the competition
top.description: OpenAI says its new AI chip, Jalapeño, completes tasks more efficiently and returns responses faster than other AI systems, according to a blog post published on Tuesday. During a briefing with report...

top.title: After Hugging Face Was Attacked By A.I. Agents, It Embarked on a Crusade
top.description: Hugging Face, a start-up that was breached by rogue bots from OpenAI, is using the hack to push for openness in A.I. development.

top.title: OpenAI’s Jalapeño chip is built for fast inference at scale, benchmarks show
top.description: Tested on SemiAnalysis’ InferenceX benchmark, Jalapeño registered both more tokens per user and more throughput per kilowatt than the currently available state-of-the art.

top.title: ‘The world seems to be ready’: An interview with OpenAI head of product Thibault Sottiaux
top.description: TechCrunch talks agents, UX, and reporting to Greg Brockman with OpenAI's head of product.
